Find the total area of the region between the curve $y={x}^{4}-1$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=2$, as shown above.
worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}-1 & =0 \\ {x}^{4} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

The only solution between $x=0$ and $x=2$ is $x=1.$

Since $1\in [0,2]$, we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=2.$

Notice that the region for $x\in [0,1]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-1)\,\text{d}x
$$

will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}-x)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-[\frac{1}{5}-1]-0 \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [1,2]$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}({x}^{4}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}-x)|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =([\frac{32}{5}-2]-[\frac{1}{5}-1]) \\  & =\frac{26}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
A={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=\frac{4}{5}+\frac{26}{5}=\frac{30}{5}=6.
$$
